source.stem:
Many molecules of J join together in reaction R to form a long chain molecule K.

K is the only product.

Which row describes molecule J, reaction R and molecule K?

options.text: molecule J: polymer; reaction R: addition; molecule K: monomer
molecule J: monomer; reaction R: addition; molecule K: polymer
molecule J: polymer; reaction R: cracking; molecule K: monomer
molecule J: monomer; reaction R: cracking; molecule K: polymer

packed_tags.subject: science
packed_tags.topic: What counts as a scientific question or test

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: 'Why does all energy do things?' is a scientific investigation question.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: 'Does sugar dissolve faster in warm or cold water?' is not scientific when investigated in a kitchen.

intelligence.enrichment: In science, curiosity becomes investigation when a question is focused enough to guide careful observation, thoughtful experimentation, and clear explanation of what is seen. Focused questions determine what can be observed, tested, and explained; unfocused curiosity does not by itself define an investigation. The learner classifies a question as scientific when it is focused enough to guide careful observation, thoughtful experimentation, and clear explanation. Any interesting why question, such as why one side of a puri is thinner, is already a scientific investigation.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Exploring the inquisitive mind. The student must decide: Decide whether a curiosity question has been made scientific by turning it into a focused question that can guide careful observation, experimentation, and explanation. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE.
